questions.answer: Not traditional TV, no. Like a lot of people my age, I've shifted almost [[entirely]] to streaming, so I watch what I want, when I want. It gives me far more control over my viewing.

All the time. They've completely [[transformed]] how I watch things. Having a huge library available whenever I want is incredibly convenient, and I honestly can't imagine going back to fixed TV schedules.

questions.q: What kind of programmes do you like?
questions.answer: I gravitate towards documentaries and the occasional gripping drama. Documentaries in particular appeal to me, because I get to relax and gain a bit of [[insight]] at the same time, which feels like time well spent.

questions.q: Did you watch much TV when you were a child?
questions.answer: Quite a lot, especially cartoons after school and cricket matches with my father. Back then the whole family gathered around one television, so watching something together was a real [[communal]] experience, which I sometimes miss.

questions.q: Do you think people watch too much TV nowadays?
questions.answer: I think screen time in general is the issue now rather than TV itself. With streaming, it's so easy to [[binge-watch]] an entire series in one weekend, and many people, including me occasionally, lose track of time completely.
